name.text: Finding the mistake in describing a shear

questiontext.text:
Rectangle ABCD, with \(A({@A0[1]@},\,{@A0[2]@})\), \(B({@B0[1]@},\,{@B0[2]@})\), \(C({@C0[1]@},\,{@C0[2]@})\) and \(D({@D0[1]@},\,{@D0[2]@})\), is mapped onto \(A'B'C'D'\), with \(A'({@A1[1]@},\,{@A1[2]@})\), \(B'({@B1[1]@},\,{@B1[2]@})\), \(C'({@C1[1]@},\,{@C1[2]@})\) and \(D'({@D1[1]@},\,{@D1[2]@})\), by a shear. Mwangi describes the shear. One step has a mistake.

  1. Points on the [[if test="is(ax=\"x\")"]]x[[else]]y[[/if]]-axis do not move, so the [[if test="is(ax=\"x\")"]]x[[else]]y[[/if]]-axis is invariant.
  2. Corner C moves \({@abs(dsh)@}\) units in the [[if test="is(dsh>0)"]]positive[[else]]negative[[/if]] [[if test="is(ax=\"x\")"]]x[[else]]y[[/if]]-direction.
  3. C is \({@h@}\) units from the [[if test="is(ax=\"x\")"]]x[[else]]y[[/if]]-axis.
  4. Shear factor = \({@sfs@}\).
  5. Matrix = \({@Msh@}\).

(a) Which step has the mistake?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Give the correct shear factor.

[[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
(a) [[if test="is(er=1)"]][[/if]][[if test="is(er=2)"]]The mistake is in Step 2. C moves from \(C({@C0[1]@},\,{@C0[2]@})\) to \(C'({@C1[1]@},\,{@C1[2]@})\), which is \({@abs(moved)@}\) units, not \({@abs(dsh)@}\).[[/if]][[if test="is(er=3)"]][[/if]][[if test="is(er=4)"]]The mistake is in Step 4. Shear factor = distance moved \(\div\) distance from the invariant axis, not the other way round.[[/if]][[if test="is(er=5)"]]The mistake is in Step 5. With the [[if test="is(ax=\"x\")"]]x[[else]]y[[/if]]-axis invariant the shear factor goes [[if test="is(ax=\"x\")"]]in the top right[[else]]in the bottom left[[/if]] of the matrix.[[/if]]

(b) Shear factor = \({@moved@} \div {@h@} = {@k@}\), and the matrix is \({@Sm@}\).

questiondescription.text:
Matrices and Transformations: finding the mistake in describing a shear

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.1: Find the wrong step in a description of a shear from a rectangle and its image, and give the correct shear factor.

Core

truefeedback.text: Step 3 is right: C is \({@h@}\) units from the axis.

falsefeedback.text: [[if test="is(ans1=\"s1\")"]]Step 1 is right: the [[if test="is(ax=\"x\")"]]y[[else]]x[[/if]]-coordinate of every corner stays the same, so the points slide parallel to the [[if test="is(ax=\"x\")"]]x[[else]]y[[/if]]-axis. [[/if]][[if test="is(ans1=\"s2\")"]]Step 2 is right: C moves from \(C({@C0[1]@},\,{@C0[2]@})\) to \(C'({@C1[1]@},\,{@C1[2]@})\), \({@abs(moved)@}\) units. [[/if]][[if test="is(ans1=\"s4\")"]]Step 4 follows from Steps 2 and 3: \({@dsh@} \div {@h@} = {@sfs@}\). [[/if]][[if test="is(ans1=\"s5\")"]]Step 5 puts the factor from Step 4 in the right place: with the [[if test="is(ax=\"x\")"]]x[[else]]y[[/if]]-axis invariant it goes [[if test="is(ax=\"x\")"]]in the top right[[else]]in the bottom left[[/if]]. [[/if]]Check each step against the coordinates: which axis stays fixed, how far C moves, how far C is from the axis, then the division and the matrix.

truefeedback.text: Shear factor = distance moved \(\div\) distance from the invariant axis, not the reverse.[[if test="is(er=4)"]] That is Mwangi's factor.[[/if]]
[[if test="is(er=2)"]]That is Mwangi's factor, which uses the wrong distance from Step 2.[[else]]That uses a distance moved one unit too far.[[/if]] Count again how far C moves.

falsefeedback.text: Shear factor = distance moved \(\div\) distance from the invariant axis, with a sign for the direction.

qtest.description: Another wrong step; distance one unit out
